ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Event-guided feature warping from a single RGB frame
PROPOSAL: Encode the frame I_t once with SegFormer-B2, then warp its stride-8 feature map to the target offset using a flow field regressed from a voxel-grid event tensor with five temporal bins. A light decoder fuses the warped features with an event branch and takes the offset as a continuous time embedding. Train on DSEC-Semantic with offsets sampled uniformly inside the gap, causal inputs only.
CONTROLS: Frame copy with no warping, constant-velocity flow extrapolated from past RGB frames, an event-only SegFormer, and ablations removing the time embedding and the event branch; three seeds each, mIoU reported per offset bucket and on moving-object classes.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: Gain over frame copy should grow with the offset, strongest on pedestrians and riders; it may fail to place objects that enter the scene after the frame, since warping cannot create content absent from the frame.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Event-conditioned cross-attention decoder for gap prediction
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune a SegFormer-B2 frame encoder jointly with an event encoder over voxel grids, and merge both streams in a cross-attention decoder queried by the offset. Run the full pipeline on DSEC-Semantic, then on DDD17 and on a CARLA-rendered event set, retraining the event encoder from scratch per dataset over five random initialisations per setting, and evaluate at twenty offsets inside the gap, logging per-class errors per offset bucket.
CONTROLS: Frame copy, an event-only network and a late-fusion variant; ablations over voxel bin count (three, five, nine) and decoder depth, each trained to convergence on all three datasets.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: Fusion should beat late fusion by a few mIoU points on moving classes; it may fail on CARLA events, whose noise statistics differ from real sensors, limiting transfer of conclusions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Time-embedded gating of frame features by event activity
PROPOSAL: Freeze a DeepLabv3+ ResNet-50 trained on Cityscapes and learn only a small gating module that reads an event count image accumulated up to t+dt and rescales the frozen frame logits per pixel, with the offset injected through a sinusoidal embedding. Training uses DSEC-Semantic day sequences and a fixed split of 20 percent for validation.
CONTROLS: Frozen frame logits with no gating, event-only logits, a gate without the offset embedding, and a gate fed by raw polarity sums; three seeds each, scored by mean intersection over union in bins of offset length.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: The gate should recover part of the loss at long offsets at tiny training cost; it may fail where objects move far from their position in I_t, since a pixelwise gate cannot relocate labels.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Distilling a bidirectional teacher into a causal event student
PROPOSAL: Train a teacher that sees both I_t and the future frame with SegFormer-B3, then distil it into a causal student that sees only I_t and events. Run the distillation on DSEC-Semantic, DDD17 and the MVSEC driving sequences, with the teacher retrained per dataset and students trained at five loss weightings and three initialisations each, evaluating at fifteen offsets in the gap and tracking validation loss at each epoch.
CONTROLS: A student trained on hard labels only, frame copy, and an event-only network; ablations removing the feature-level loss and removing the teacher's temporal context, on each dataset.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: Distillation should lift the student on moving classes relative to hard labels; it may fail on MVSEC, where the labels are sparse and noisy and the teacher supervises poorly.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Latent neural ODE for semantic evolution inside the gap
PROPOSAL: Compress I_t into a latent map with a Mask2Former pixel decoder and evolve it forward in continuous time with a neural ODE whose vector field is conditioned on features of the event stream; decode at the queried offset. Train on DSEC-Semantic with a causal curriculum, first short offsets then the whole gap, using the adjoint method for memory and a fixed-step solver at test time.
CONTROLS: A discrete-step recurrent model, frame copy, flow-warping from events, and a variant with the field conditioned on the frame only; ablations on solver step size and on event feature depth, three seeds, with per-class intersection over union at three offsets.
COST: 480
PREDICTION: The continuous model should interpolate offsets unseen in training better than a discrete recurrence; it may fail in dense traffic where the learned field drifts and errors compound with offset.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical query propagation with a bank of event encoders
PROPOSAL: Propagate Mask2Former object queries from I_t to the target time using event-derived motion tokens. Build the system on DSEC-Semantic and M3ED, with six event encoders (voxel grid, time surface, event frame, two learned tokenisers, a point-cloud variant) each paired with two query decoders and trained to convergence for three seeds, then select the best pairing per dataset using the test split offsets and report the confusion matrix of each selected model at three offset buckets.
CONTROLS: Frame copy, event-only Mask2Former, a mask-warping baseline from optical flow, and ablations removing query propagation and removing motion tokens, evaluated per encoder pairing.
COST: 480
PREDICTION: Query propagation should help most on thing classes and abrupt appearances; it may fail for stuff classes, whose masks are better handled by dense warping than by query updates.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Offset-aware linear probing of event features on a frozen backbone
PROPOSAL: Keep a SegFormer-B1 frame model frozen and train only a 1x1 convolutional head on concatenated frame features and a time-surface encoding of events, with the offset supplied as two channels of sine and cosine. Use the DSEC-Semantic training sequences, restricted to the 11 classes shared with Cityscapes, and report on the standard validation split.
CONTROLS: Frame copy, a head on frame features alone, a head on events alone and a head without the offset channels; three seeds each, mean intersection over union reported per offset bucket.
COST: 36
PREDICTION: Even a linear head should beat frame copy once the offset exceeds half the gap; it may fail to segment thin structures such as poles, whose detail is removed by the coarse stride and cannot be restored by events.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Pretraining an event backbone on synthetic gap sequences
PROPOSAL: Render driving sequences in CARLA at high frame rate with ground-truth semantics, convert them into events with a simulator, and pretrain an event backbone to predict maps at random offsets from a single frame. Fine-tune on DSEC-Semantic and DDD17, repeating pretraining with 3 seeds and 3 rendering weather sets, and compare initialisations at 10 offsets inside the gap with one run per combination and a plot of the validation curve.
CONTROLS: Training from scratch, ImageNet initialisation, and pretraining on frame-only synthetic data; ablations removing the event simulator noise model and the weather variety.
COST: 36
PREDICTION: Pretraining should help most with little real data; it may fail where the simulator's event noise differs from real sensors, giving no gain over ImageNet initialisation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Anytime prediction with a state-space temporal model over events
PROPOSAL: Process the event stream in microsecond-ordered chunks with a Mamba-style state-space model which carries a recurrent state initialised from the encoded frame I_t, and read out a segmentation map from the state at any offset. Train on DSEC-Semantic and M3ED with truncated sequences first, then full gap lengths, with SegFormer-B2 as the frame encoder and stride-8 outputs.
CONTROLS: A transformer over event tokens at matched parameters, a recurrent convolutional network, frame copy and event-only prediction; ablations on state size, chunk length and initialisation from the frame, with three seeds and mIoU at five offsets.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: The state-space model should keep accuracy flat with offset better than the convolutional recurrence; it may fail on the drone sequences where ego-motion is large and the initial state quickly becomes stale.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Offset-conditioned diffusion decoder on top of event features
PROPOSAL: Condition a latent diffusion decoder on the frame encoding and event features, sampling a semantic map at the requested offset. Train on DSEC-Semantic, then on M3ED drone and quadruped sequences, with samplers of 10, 25 and 50 steps, five seeds, and a fresh encoder per dataset; evaluate each model at fifteen offsets and with eight samples per input to estimate calibration and a reliability curve per class.
CONTROLS: A deterministic decoder of the same size, frame copy, plus an event-only diffusion model; ablations over sampler steps and over the conditioning mask on events, per dataset.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: The diffusion decoder should give better calibrated maps on ambiguous regions; it may be unable to improve mIoU over the deterministic decoder, and its sampling latency may be too high for a vehicle.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Class-wise motion priors combined with event flow
PROPOSAL: Estimate dense flow from events with a small RAFT-style network, then move each class region of the SegFormer-B2 prediction for the input frame by a class-specific motion model, rigid for vehicles and articulated for people, learned on DSEC-Semantic. Disocclusions are filled by the event-conditioned decoder at the target offset. Training is two-stage: flow network first, then fill-in decoder.
CONTROLS: Uniform flow warping, frame copy, an event-only model, and a version without class-specific motion; three seeds, with per-class intersection over union and boundary F-score at three offsets.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: Class-specific motion should help vehicles and riders; it may fail to follow pedestrians who change direction abruptly, because the motion model predicts the wrong displacement.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Choosing the event representation for gap prediction
PROPOSAL: Compare eight event representations for anytime segmentation from one frame, among them voxel grids with three, five and nine bins, time surfaces, event frames and learned tokenisers, each paired with SegFormer-B2 and trained on DSEC-Semantic, then re-trained on DDD17. Each representation is trained over five seeds and scored at ten offsets in the gap, to rank them for the causal setting and to list the strongest one per class.
CONTROLS: Frame copy and an event-only model per representation; ablations dropping the frame and dropping polarity, evaluated on both datasets with matching schedules.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: Learned tokenisers should rank first at long offsets; the ranking may fail to carry over between datasets because the sensors differ in resolution and contrast thresholds.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cheap anytime refinement of a frame prediction with event residuals
PROPOSAL: Run SegFormer-B2 on I_t once and train a residual head which corrects its logits using an event frame accumulated up to the target time, conditioned on the offset by feature-wise modulation. Training uses the DSEC-Semantic training sequences with random offsets, and the head has under one million parameters so it can run at event arrival rate on embedded hardware.
CONTROLS: Frame copy, residual head without offset modulation, residual head on polarity-free events, and a full fine-tune of the encoder; three seeds, mIoU by offset bucket and per class.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: The residual head should capture most of the gain of a full fine-tune at a fraction of its training; it may fail on classes whose appearance changes, such as traffic lights, which need new content.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cross-dataset study of causal event fusion at scale
PROPOSAL: Evaluate a SegFormer-B3 fusion model with a time-conditioned decoder on eight datasets, DSEC-Semantic, DDD17, MVSEC and M3ED, training on each and testing on all, over five random seeds per pair and offsets sampled at twenty positions. Report a full transfer matrix of mean intersection over union, and fit a regression from dataset statistics such as event rate to the transfer loss, with a bootstrap interval per entry.
CONTROLS: Frame copy plus an event-only model on each target, and ablations removing the frame branch and removing the offset conditioning; the transfer matrix is repeated per ablation.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Transfer should degrade with the gap in event rate between datasets; the regression may fail with only eight datasets, giving unstable coefficients.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Mask-token propagation for objects that appear after the frame
PROPOSAL: Add learned appearance tokens to a Mask2Former decoder: tokens seeded from the frame carry known objects, and tokens spawned from clusters of events carry objects absent from the frame. At the queried offset both sets decode into the semantic map. Train on DSEC-Semantic with a sampler that oversamples clips where a pedestrian enters the scene, and with synthetic insertions of moving shapes.
CONTROLS: Mask2Former on frame copy, an event-only version, a model with seeded tokens only, and one with event tokens only; three seeds, with recall of newly appearing objects and mean intersection over union at three offsets.
COST: 320
PREDICTION: Event tokens should recover appearing pedestrians that frame-seeded tokens miss; it may fail when events from background motion trigger false tokens, hurting precision.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Horizon-specific event-conditioned decoders for gap prediction
PROPOSAL: Train SegFormer-B2 fusion models for twelve gap lengths from a few milliseconds to the full interval, on DSEC-Semantic, DDD17 and MVSEC, with a separate model per length and five seeds, then test each model at all offsets inside its horizon. Use a cosine schedule with long warmup and select the checkpoint on each dataset's own validation split after logging mIoU at each epoch.
CONTROLS: A single model trained with random offsets, frame copy and an event-only network at each horizon; ablations on the event window before t, using three window lengths per dataset.
COST: 320
PREDICTION: Horizon-specific models should win at their own length by small amounts; the single anytime model may match them, so that separate training per length brings nothing.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Event-conditioned video prediction in latent space for segmentation
PROPOSAL: Predict future latent features of a frozen video encoder from the I_t latent and event tokens with a causal transformer, then decode a semantic map from the predicted latent at the queried offset using a lightweight head. Pretrain the predictor on unlabelled DSEC and M3ED event streams with masked latent loss, then fine-tune the head on DSEC-Semantic labels.
CONTROLS: Direct fine-tuning without latent prediction, frame copy, an optical-flow warp of latents, and a predictor without events; ablations on predictor depth and mask ratio, three seeds, mIoU at five offsets.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: Self-supervised latent prediction should improve long offsets with few labels; it may fail if the frozen encoder discards fine spatial detail which the head needs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Augmentation recipes for an event-conditioned decoder
PROPOSAL: Train a SegFormer-B2 event fusion model on DSEC-Semantic under a Cartesian product of augmentations: five brightness curves, four event noise levels, three flip settings and four random-crop scales, giving 240 training recipes, then repeat the best twenty recipes over five seeds each on DDD17 and MVSEC, scoring each model at ten offsets and listing the mIoU of each recipe against its training loss.
CONTROLS: Frame copy plus an event-only network per recipe, and ablations removing the time embedding; each recipe is retrained without events to isolate their contribution.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: Noise augmentation should matter most for robustness to event rate; the grid may fail to find a recipe that beats the default by more than seed variance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Boundary refinement from events after frame warping
PROPOSAL: Warp the SegFormer-B2 map of the frame by an event-estimated flow, then refine object boundaries with a small network that reads event edge maps in a window around each warped contour. The refiner is trained on DSEC-Semantic with a boundary-weighted loss and receives the offset as a scalar channel; only the refiner and the flow estimator are trained.
CONTROLS: Plain warping, frame copy, a refiner without event edges, and an event-only boundary predictor; three seeds, boundary F-score within 2 pixels and mean intersection over union by offset bucket.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Event edges should sharpen contours of moving vehicles at long offsets; refinement may fail on static classes where the warp is already exact.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-scale event pyramid with five encoders and ensembling
PROPOSAL: Build five event pyramids with different temporal resolutions and train a separate SegFormer-B2 fusion network on each over DSEC-Semantic, M3ED and MVSEC, using three seeds apiece, then combine the fifteen models per dataset with learned weights fitted at twelve offsets. Compare ensemble members and report the contribution of each resolution to the ensemble and the overlap of their errors.
CONTROLS: A single-resolution model, frame copy, and an event-only network; ablations on ensemble size (one, three, five, fifteen) and weight fitting method per dataset.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: The ensemble should add a point or two of mIoU over the best member; it may not justify its inference cost for an anytime deployment.
